recipes.name: Vegetarian Tater Tot Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.5 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Arrange tater tots in the prepared baking dish.
Combine sour cream, cheese, and condensed soup in a mixing bowl. Pour this mixture over tater tots. Sprinkle onions over the top of the casserole.
Bake in the preheated oven for 45 to 60 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Vegetarian Tater Tot Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This is a recipe for tater tot casserole without meat that everyone will love — vegetarian or not. Simply bake tots, cheese, and mushroom soup.

review.reviewBody:
this is officially my new favorite recipe! i did make a few changes to improve it slightly in my book. i used extra crispy tater tots (instead of regular tots), used fat free knudsens brand sour cream and 98% fat free cream of chicken soup. i used sharp cheddar 
and doubled the recommended amount (i love cheese!). i also bought the larger can of french fried onions and mixed 1/2 in with the soup, sc, and cheese mixture. once the mixture is spread over the tots, i sprinkled with garlic powder and finished it off with the last of the ff onions. super easy and heats up great for leftovers! yummmm....

The ultimate in comfort food! This dish brings me back to my childhood...even my college sorority cook made this. This version is definitely better. After finding this recipe and making this many, many times now, I make the following changes: brown a pound of 93/7 hamburger, seasoned with garlic powder, pepper, and half an onion; no grease to drain! I brown an entire bag of crispy crowns instead of regular tots. I layer the hamburger meat over the crispy crowns, then spread the soup mixture, which incorporates the top reviewer's suggestion to add more sharp cheddar than called for, some French fried onions, and I also season the mixture with additional spices to my liking (garlic & onion powders, a little paprika and pepper). I also use the Roasted Garlic Cream of Mushroom soup and the entire 16 oz container of sour cream. It's thick and creamy and using the back of a spoon, it spreads easier than you think. So what if the hamburger is mixed in? Top that with some additional cheese and bake 35-40 minutes at 350. 1-2 minutes before it's done, I sprinkle a few more French fried onions on the top and turn the oven to broil. After taking it out, let it sit for 10 minutes. Perfection! Now, if only my husband would let me add some green beans to the mix....

My husband and my two toddlers absolutely loved this casserole. I believe my husband even had three helpings.

I added extra cheese on top before the fried onions because we love cheese. I also added in frozen broccoli for some veggies. This was so good with ketchup (in my house we love ketchup too). 

It is extremely rich and heavy but so good. I would pair it with a salad or steamed veggies or even some grilled chicken.

When I make it again, which I will, instead of just pouring the mixture on top, I will mix it into the tater tots because some of the bottom ones weren’t smothered.

I used curly fries instead of tater tots. I sprinkled onion powder, garlic powder and paprika onto the fries in the dish. I added 2 small cans of drained chicken and used cream of chicken soup instead of cream of mushroom. Otherwise followed recipe. The cream soup mixture kind of stayed on top when baked. Maybe press it into the fries next time or keep some of the chicken broth from the canned chicken. It was very good.

I did everything just like the recipe stated - exactly - but It was awful. First off, the tots were cold inside. Second, the gloopy “sauce” stayed gloopy. It did not thin out to run in between the potatoes and just stayed on top like a hat. The onions on top charred. Taste was also rather one sided - sour cream. You couldn’t taste the mushroom soup at all, nor any of the cheese, as it was overshadowed by the sour cream. If I were to ever try this again, I would make a mushroom sauce from scratch with a Béchamel base and make sure it coated all the tots. The onions would go on top towards the end of the baking, along with some extra cheese to give it a bit more flavor. Not a fan of this, though.

I have made this many times since discovering the recipe. It is great as is but usually I add or substitute a few things. I use onion flavored tater tots for a little extra oomph to the dish. For the cream of mushroom soup I have used cream of chicken, celery or onion on occasion. They all tasted fantastic! I also add a can of french sliced green beans (drained) to the sauce mix. It lets me imagine that its a little bit healthier and the flavors go well together! I also add a tiny bit of milk to thin the sauce out just a bit so it can get inbetween all the tater tots and not sit on top of them. Overall an awesome recipe!

This is one of my favorite “I don’t wanna cook” recipes to make. It’s so easy to make it takes about two minutes to prep. After some attempts I swapped out the cream of mushroom for a good, buttermilk-based ranch (Ocharleys or litehouse) and added a layer of American Cheese over the top (before adding the onions). I feel like there is a lot you could do to this (bacon, broccoli, shredded chicken or beef) but it’s perfectly great as is. This doubles as a good family comfort meal or the office/church potluck hit.

Changes I made were sauteing fresh mushrooms in a combination of olive oil and butter, adding about 2 TBS of flour to the mixture once the mushrooms were brown and adding milk until thick. As for the rest of the recipe I followed to the letter, The whole family loved it eve my picky eater.

This was stellar. The only reason it did not get 5 stars is that there was some modifications required. First off: Brown a pound of burger with some onions. I used a third of a red onion and that was enough. Double the cheese in the mix in the bowl. I used probably 2/3 of the recommended amount of sour cream. Use more or less. Either way will be fine.

Drop the burger in the bowl and stir. Add 1/2 the french fried onions when done mixing the burger in the bowl. Spoon and spread the mix in the pan and cover the tots. Spread the remaining FF onions over the top. Sixty minutes plus 10 was required at 350. Make this. You will not regret it!

I only made one change... I substituted plain Greek yogurt for about half of the sour cream. Their consistency is so similar and the yogurt adds protein. It was fantastic! And so easy to put together! Next time I plan to bake at 400 instead of 350. I thought it cooled down very quickly.

Just made it tonight as a meatless dish for Lent. I did make some changes. I cooked it as per the directions, only covered; after 50 minutes, I uncovered, added the extra cheese and the French onions in layers; then threw it in the oven, uncovered, for about more 15 minutes. I made the following modifications: - Reduced the amount of Sour Cream to 8oz. + Doubled (tripled?) the amount of cheese, we like cheese! Just kept adding cheese until "it looked right." + 1/2 cup of milk + 2/3 cup of sweet peas + 1/2 TBSP of Garlic Powder + 1/2 tsp of Cayanne Pepper. Results: It was pretty good. To me, it tasted like loaded tots, the mixture wasn't absorbed by the tots, and the onions on the top provided the extra goodness of crunch, and the peas...just made it special. It won't be in the weekly rotation; but it is good for special occasions as or meatless days.

I made something similar. I use cheddar broccoli soup instead of cream of mushroom soup, and I added some steamed broccoli. My vegetarian daughter loves it, and like when I make it when she is visiting.

I think the recipe is great like it is. To the people suggesting to add beef… this is a vegetarian recipe!!! It’s pretty silly to suggest adding beef to a recipe with vegetarian in the title. There are plenty of recipes that already include the beef version.

This is quite delicious, but my husband said, "Let's not make this for dinner again - it's not great for us." True! If we make it again, it will definitely be as a side dish to take to a family holiday potluck where nobody expects the food to be healthy. If we make it again as a vegetarian main course, we'll cut the sour cream in half and sprinkle green onions on top instead of the friend onions (although my daughter said to that idea, "Really? Those friend onions are definitely the best part."). Oh, and we might add some veggie sausage too.

I made some small changes. I used French onion dip instead of sour cream. I used more cheese and added a layer of cheese on the top in the last 15 minutes and I mixed French fried onions in with the mixture amd added frozen peas. Also, many people mentioned it being a glob on the top. I used cream of onion soup because I'm allergic to mushrooms. I figured maybe the recipe should have called for the soup, prepared, rather than just what was in the can, so I added a can of water and it was the perfect consistency. My family gobbled this up.
Added garlic pepper and chopped onions; omitted the fried onions. Halved the recipe in an 11x7 pan, cooked 40 minutes. Ideal for an easy, quick side dish.
I made it according to the directions, except I use sweet potato tater tots. The taste was really good however, after baking for an hour at 3:50, the bottom of the casserole dish was still cold.
They tasted ok but the cheese and sour cream mixture is too thick, even with can of soup added. The cooked combination had an odd texture. Wish it were more blended and saucy.
Quick and easy, mixed it up threw it in the oven gave the kiddo a bath and when she was done so was the casserole. Next time I make it I’m going to add chicken and peas.
It was so easy, quick. It needed something for flavor…
